question.problem: Solve for $C$ given that $y(t) = C \cdot \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{t}$ and $y(5)=1.$
question.worked_solution:
We substitute $t=5$ and $y(t)=1$ into the expression for $y(t),$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}1 & =C\cdot {(\frac{1}{2})}^{5} \\ 1 & =C\cdot \frac{{1}^{5}}{{2}^{5}} \\ 1 & =C\cdot \frac{1}{32} \\ 1\cdot 32 & =C \\ 32 & =C.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $C=32.$
